findings.title: enableSqlExpressions always returns false and unconditionally dereferences feature toggles
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as the negation of IsEnabledGlobally(FlagSqlExpressions), then returns false on both branches, so the helper is dead, inverted-looking logic. It also unconditionally calls h.features.IsEnabledGlobally even though the result is discarded; an ExpressionQueryReader constructed with a nil FeatureToggles (as test and non-service callers can do) will panic on a SQL query instead of returning the intended 'not implemented' error. Replace the helper with an explicit unconditional rejection (or a nil-safe check) so the disablement is clear and cannot be accidentally re-enabled by 'fixing' one branch.

findings.title: Legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path is not explicitly gated like the reader path
findings.body: The explicit SQL-expression rejection was added only to ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery in pkg/expr/reader.go. UnmarshalSQLCommand (the legacy rawNode unmarshalling path used by the older SSE pipeline) still calls NewSQLCommand with no disabled/feature check; it is currently blocked only incidentally because the stubbed sql.TablesList returns a generic 'not implemented' error, which surfaces as a misleading 'error reading SQL command' BadRequest. If TablesList/the stub DB is ever restored or changed, this entry point silently becomes reachable again. Add the same explicit rejection to UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand as defense-in-depth for CVE-2024-9264.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions are rejected on all entry points
findings.body: This security change adds no test asserting that QueryTypeSQL is rejected when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled, nor that the legacy UnmarshalSQLCommand path is rejected, and it does not update the existing SQL-expression tests that exercise NewSQLCommand/TablesList/Execute (which now always fail via the stub DB). Without a regression test, a future refactor of enableSqlExpressions or the stub DB could re-enable the DuckDB-backed RCE/LFI surface unnoticed, and the current test suite is left failing or must be silently skipped. Add CVE regression tests for both parsing entry points and update/skip the obsolete happy-path SQL tests explicitly.
